assessments.mechanism: Intrinsic prompted self-correction without reliable external correctness feedback can degrade reasoning.
assessments.clean_scope: Matched GSM8K/CommonSenseQA/HotpotQA tests on specified GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Llama-2-era models; not evidence against correction with external verifiers or newer specialized systems.
assessments.o_comparison: O's repair loop uses task evidence and fresh Root cycles rather than assuming intrinsic self-correction, but no matched intrinsic-self-correction experiment was found. The clean result should therefore not be treated as an O-evaluated failure.

assessments.mechanism: Homogeneous multi-agent debate can lose to equal-response self-consistency at matched response budget.
assessments.clean_scope: Specific gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 GSM8K setup with 3 agents/2 rounds; does not reject heterogeneous/specialized MAS.
assessments.o_comparison: No multi-agent debate implementation/evaluation was found in O; exact-code search for the phrase multi-agent returned no direct design hit.

assessments.mechanism: Search-time access to benchmark answers/metadata can inflate search-agent benchmark scores.
assessments.clean_scope: Public benchmark/search infrastructure contamination; leakage rates are environment/benchmark-specific and not transferable to private/dynamic tests.
assessments.o_comparison: O already uses secret-seeded/redacted held-out tasks, disclosure tracking, label-separated scorer access, contamination-aware fresh executors, and explicit provenance. It has not measured web search-time answer leakage for the cited public benchmarks/retrievers.

assessments.mechanism: Reusable agent skills can cause functional and efficiency regressions; attribute them with paired no-skill/cheaper controls.
assessments.clean_scope: SkillsBench/SWE-Skills-Bench paired-counterfactual preprint; benchmark and implementation specific.
assessments.o_comparison: O's Candidate lifecycle is scoped/reversible, preserves a protected control, tracks cost/risk, and does not activate untested candidates globally. It has not reproduced the cited skill-regression taxonomy or paired skill/no-skill benchmark.

assessments.mechanism: Full execution traces can materially improve failure attribution compared with partial observations in multi-agent systems.
assessments.clean_scope: TraceElephant multi-agent attribution benchmark; this is attribution evidence, not direct task-success evidence.
assessments.o_comparison: O persists detailed invocation/tool events, provenance, outcomes, and immutable journals rather than final outputs only. It has not run a full-vs-partial trace attribution experiment or a multi-agent attribution benchmark.

assessments.mechanism: Benchmark defects can masquerade as agent failures; benchmark auditing should be treated as a first-class validity check.
assessments.clean_scope: BenchGuard evidence is on ScienceAgentBench and BIXBench Verified-50; no inference about other benchmarks without task-level audit.
assessments.o_comparison: O explicitly treats repository-authored generators/scorers as possible false-positive paths, keeps reference passes non-claim-grade, and uses hidden/redacted scoring contracts. It does not implement an automated BenchGuard-like defect auditor or measure author-confirmed defect recall.
